correctness.rationale: H(x,y)=(1+κx²)(1+κy²) is an exact first integral with smooth closed nonzero levels, so physical-time periodicity holds. The exact quarter time change gives |dt|=L*g(Lw)*g(L(1−w))dw/(2sqrt Q), g(s)=(1−e^{−s})^(−1/2), and I_L=1+4log2/L+o(1/L) because integral_0^∞(g−1)=2log2 and the two boundary layers decouple. Monotonicity of log g derivative makes h_L have one mean-density crossing on each side. Its moving crossing w_L→0 but Lw_L→infinity, so one boundary mass gives L sup|F_L−id|→2log2; the inverse CDF phase has same sharp constant. Four-fold symmetry yields exact dTV=2 max(F_L−id) and therefore 4log2. Independent high precision time-density quadrature at L=8,16,32 reproduced L(I_L−1)=2.7733246,2.7725892,2.7725887 approaching 4log2; finite values are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: Llibre–Rondón Theorem 2(a) proves global-center existence for this subfamily and classical complete elliptic integral asymptotics yield its period. The present claimed new statements are sharp UNIFORM full-phase deviation and total-variation original-time occupation constants, not mere center existence or the period. Closest published asymmetric beta-layer theory explicitly excludes q=1 and states only leading weak limits in a varying-coefficient crossover, without these balanced sharp 1/L phase and TV constants. The other high-energy occupation theorem reviewed in full is a different polynomial Hamiltonian family. Residual overlap with classical incomplete elliptic integrals cannot be ruled out.
residual_risks: A transformed incomplete-elliptic-integral asymptotic could have recorded the sharp boundary-layer constants under other terminology.
The amplitude limit is for fixed κ>0; no uniform κ→0 statement.

value.rationale: A global nonlinear oscillator can be described beyond orbit closure by its full normalized physical-time energy-transfer waveform and stationary occupation statistics; these sharp error constants give quantitative control of a natural limiting shape. The nontrivial boundary layer, particularly TV rather than weak convergence, is valuable even though the elliptic period is classical.

limitations: The period formula is classical, not the standalone novelty.
No generalization to all cubic global-center families or perturbation robustness.
